properties.name: Pillar Creek
properties.species: pink salmon, coho salmon, Dolly Varden
properties.timing: Pink salmon arrive in July and run through mid-September. The coho salmon run begins in August and continues through October. Dolly Varden can be found from July through the winter months.
properties.desc: A short, tidally influenced river. Popular among coho and pink salmon anglers for surf casting.
properties.access: Access from the unimproved road that leads down to the river mouth or directly across from Pillar Creek Hatchery at the culvert. Fishing takes place at river mouth, in several holes along the river, or at the culvert just below the highway. Anglers also cast into the ocean along the beach at the river mouth.
properties.getting: North from Kodiak on Rezanof Drive and continue onto Monashka Bay Road. Continue 7.5 miles to Pillar Creek Hatchery.
properties.parking: Parking area just past Pillar Creek Hatchery on the right side of the road.  Or, continue 1 mile and park in the small lot on the right. The unimproved road leads down to the river mouth.
properties.tackle:
For coho salmon, spin anglers should try a 6 to 7 foot medium-to-heavy action rod outfitted with 12 to 20 pound test line. Coho salmon will usually strike at most bright and flashy lures, especially Vibrax (No. 3 or No. 4). Green, purple, pink, and orange are popular colors. Cured salmon eggs drifted in the current or fished with a bobber can be highly effective for catching coho salmon, and often produce bites when fish are being finicky. 

Pink salmon will readily take lures, eggs, and flies. Use lightweight spinning gear or a 4 to 5wt fly rod. Popular lures include small Pixees, larger Vibrax or Mepps spinners, or any bright and flashy fly.

For Dolly Varden, a 6 to 8 foot light-action rod with 6 pound test line works well. Small spinners and beads (No. 0, 1 or 2) are popular. Fly anglers commonly use a 3 to 5wt fly rod with leech or alevin flies.

properties.name: Buskin Lake
properties.species: Dolly Varden, steelhead trout, rainbow trout, coho salmon
properties.timing: The coho salmon run begins in mid-August and continues through early October, with the run peaking in mid-September.  Dolly Varden and rainbow trout can be present year round with Dolly Varden most abundant in April-May and July-October. Steelhead arrive in early October and are present through May.
properties.desc: A large lake for the road system can be fished from shore or by non-motorized boat.
properties.access: Access from a spur road off of Anton Larsen Bay Road at the last Buskin River Bridge or a trail that borders the driving range at the Golf Course on Anton Larsen Bay Road.
properties.getting: South from Kodiak on Rezanof Dr. Turn right onto Anton Larsen Bay Road and continue ~1.5 miles.
properties.parking: Parking lot at lake outlet or park at Bear Valley Golf Course driving range.
properties.tackle:
Spin anglers should try a 6 to 7 foot medium-to-heavy action rod outfitted with 12 to 20 pound test line. Coho salmon will usually strike at most bright and flashy lures, especially Vibrax (No. 3 or 4). Green, purple, pink, and orange are popular colors. Cured salmon eggs drifted in the current or fished with a bobber can be highly effective for catching coho salmon, and often produce bites when fish are being finicky. For fly fishing, an 8 to 9wt fly rod is the best option. Use a sinking tip or shooting head floating line for in river fishing or a floating line with weighted flies for still water fishing. 

For steelhead and rainbow trout, spin anglers should try a 6 to 8 foot medium-action rod with 10 to 12 pound test line. Spoons and spinners are effective, along with salmon eggs and egg-pattern yarn flies drifted in swift water with a weighted and swiveled 12 to 18 inch leader. Fly anglers commonly use sinking tip lines or floating lines with weighted flies on a 6wt fly rod.
properties.eo: ADF&G listed a 2026 emergency order (Jun 22): Buskin River closed to sport fishing for sockeye salmon. Check the EO list for current status.

properties.name: Dog Salmon River/Frazer Lake drainage
properties.species: king salmon, sockeye salmon, pink salmon, chum salmon, coho salmon, dolly varden, arctic char, rainbow trout, steelhead
properties.timing: Sockeye salmon start their run in mid-May and run through September. King salmon arrive in May and run through late-July. Pinks arrive near the end of July and run through mid-September. Coho start showing up in August and run through October. Dolly Varden, arctic char and rainbow trout can be found from July through the winter months and into May. Steelhead run from late-September through November and can be found into May.
properties.desc: Located on the south end of the island, the Dog Salmon River hosts a man-made sockeye salmon run via a fish pass around barrier waterfalls. It flows from Frazer Lake and is also popular for bear viewing.
properties.access: Access is either to Olga Bay at the mouth of the river or Frazer Lake via float plane.
properties.getting: Access is primarily via floatplane.
properties.parking: None
properties.tackle: Spin fishing anglers targeting king, pink, or coho salmon should try using a 6- to 7-foot medium-action rod outfitted with 8- to 12-pound test line. Vibrax® spinners, Pixee® spoons, and cured salmon roe are effective. Chunks of herring beneath a bobber or drifting along the bottom can be hard for coho and king salmon to resist. Fly fishing anglers targeting coho and king salmon should try using purple or bright green leeches. For Dolly Varden, spin anglers should try smaller Vibrax® spinners or Pixee® spoons. Fly fishing anglers should try green leeches or a Dolly Llama fly. For rainbow trout and steelhead, bead setups can be very effective, along with darker colored spinners (such as blue) or flies.

For coho salmon, spin anglers should try a 6 to 7 foot medium-to-heavy action rod outfitted with 12 to 20 pound test line. Coho salmon will usually strike at most bright and flashy lures, especially Vibrax (No. 3 or No. 4). Cured salmon eggs drifted in the current or fished with a bobber can be highly effective for catching coho salmon, and often produce bites when fish are being finicky. 
Pink salmon will readily take lures, eggs, and flies. Use lightweight spinning gear or a 4 to 5wt fly rod. Popular lures include small Pixees, larger Vibrax or Mepps spinners, or any bright and flashy fly.
For Dolly Varden, a 6 to 8 foot light-action rod with 6 pound test line works well.

Coho salmon will usually strike at most bright and flashy lures, especially Vibrax (No. 3 or No. 4). Green, purple, pink, and orange are popular colors. Cured salmon eggs drifted in the current or fished with a bobber can be highly effective for catching coho salmon, and often produce bites when fish are being finicky. 

Pink salmon will readily take lures, eggs, and flies. Use lightweight spinning gear or a 4 to 5wt fly rod. Popular lures include small Pixees, larger Vibrax or Mepps spinners, or any bright and flashy fly.

For Dolly Varden, a 6 to 8 foot light-action rod with 6 pound test line works well. Small spinners and beads (No. 0, 1 or 2) are popular. Fly anglers commonly use a 3 to 5wt fly rod with leech or alevin flies.

properties.tackle:
For sockeye salmon, spin anglers should try a 6 to 7 foot medium action rod outfitted with 8 to 12 pound test line. Most use yarn flies on a 12 to 18 inch leader attached to a swivel and weighted drop line. Fly fishers use a 6 to 8wt rod and reel outfitted with sinking tip. A number of fly patterns are used for sockeye salmon. Some anglers claim flies with chartreuse (fluorescent green) or red bodies can be particularly effective.
For coho salmon, spin anglers should try a 6 to 7 foot medium-to-heavy action rod outfitted with 12 to 20 pound test line. Coho salmon will usually strike at most bright and flashy lures, especially Vibrax (No. 3 or No. 4). Green, purple, pink, and orange are popular colors. Use lightweight spinning gear or a 4 to 5wt fly rod. Popular lures include small Pixees, larger Vibrax or Mepps spinners, or any bright and flashy fly. For rainbow trout, spin anglers should try a 6 to 8 foot medium-action rod with 10 to12 pound test line.

properties.name: Pasagshak River
properties.species: sockeye salmon, coho salmon
properties.timing: The sockeye salmon run starts in mid to late June, peaks in mid-July, and typically is over by August. The coho salmon run starts in August and continues through October.
properties.desc: A short, tidal river popular with sockeye and coho anglers. Most fishing takes place in the lower 1/4 mile for sockeye and in Lake Rose Teed for coho.
properties.access: Lake Rose Teed, which borders the Pasagshak State Recreation Area, provides a unique opportunity for anglers with access to a float tube, kayak, or small watercraft. Coho salmon hold in the lake before migrating into the upper tributaries.
properties.getting: South from Kodiak on Rezanof Dr. and continue onto Chiniak Highway. At Mile 30, head south on Pasagshak Road. Entrance to Pasagshak State Recreation Site is on the right after 9 miles.
properties.parking: Parking lot for vehicles. Several access points from Pasagshak Road to Lake Rose Teed via gravel trails as well as the lower river in the Pasagshak State Recreation Area.
properties.tackle:
For coho salmon, spin anglers should try a 6 to 7 foot medium-to-heavy action rod outfitted with 12 to 20 pound test line. Coho salmon will usually strike at most bright and flashy lures, especially Vibrax (No. 3 or No. 4). Cured salmon eggs drifted in the current or fished with a bobber can be highly effective for catching coho salmon, and often produce bites when fish are being finicky. For fly fishing, an 8 to 9wt fly rod is the best option. Use a sinking tip or shooting head floating line for in river fishing or a floating line with weighted flies for still water fishing. Purple Egg Sucking Leeches are a fly fishing favorite for coho salmon, although a wide variety of colorful and highly visible patterns will also produce fish.
For sockeye salmon, spin anglers should try a 6 to 7 foot medium action rod outfitted with 8 to 12 pound test line. Most anglers use yarn flies on a 12 to 18 inch leader attached to a swivel and weighted drop line.

properties.name: Chiniak Bay
properties.species: halibut, lingcod, rockfish, pacific cod, king salmon, coho salmon
properties.timing: Halibut are primarily targeted from May through September. Lingcod are caught from July 1st through October. Rockfish can be found year-round but mostly caught during the summer months. King salmon and Pacific cod are found year-round. Coho salmon are caught from the first week of July and peak fishing occurs in the first half of August.
properties.desc: Easily accessible saltwater fisheries are found minutes out of the boat harbor. Popular areas within Chiniak Bay include Buoy 4, Cape Chiniak and waters surrounding Long, Woody, and Spruce Islands.
properties.access: Access is from one of two harbors in the City of Kodiak or one found on the US Coast Guard Base. Some fishing is available from shore. Access is also from a number of charter boats in the City of Kodiak.
properties.getting: Access is by boat.
properties.parking: None
properties.tackle: Anglers targeting king salmon by trolling should try apex spoons (blue or green are effective). Anglers targeting coho salmon by trolling should try apex or fin fighter spoons. Anglers can also mooch for coho by using jigs - "crippled herring" work well, or try green, blue, or white jigs. Halibut, lingcod and cod anglers should try using larger jigs or with bait such as herring. White jigs are particularly effective for both species. Rockfish can be caught using smaller jigs. "Crippled herring" work well for rockfish.

properties.name: American River
properties.species: king salmon, pink salmon, chum salmon, coho salmon, Dolly Varden
properties.timing: The king salmon run begins in late June and continues through early August, though run sizes have been highly variable recently. Pink and chum salmon arrive in July and run through mid-September. The coho salmon run begins in August and continues through October. Dolly Varden can be found from July through the winter months.
properties.desc: A long, dynamic stream with many access locations. Popular river for anglers targeting king salmon, coho salmon, and Dolly Varden.
properties.access: Multiple access points on the right along the Saltery Cove trail and downstream of the American River bridge.
properties.getting: South from Kodiak on Rezanof Dr. and continue onto Chiniak Highway. Continue 20.3 miles to the bridge at the American River.
properties.parking: Parking at the American River bridge or in the Saltery Cove access trail parking lot.
properties.tackle:
For king salmon, a 7 to 8 foot heavy-action rod with 15 to 30 pound test line works well. Vibrax® spinners, Pixee® spoons, and cured salmon roe are effective. Fly fishing anglers targeting  king salmon should try using a 9 weight fly rod. 
For coho salmon, spin anglers should try a 6 to 7 foot medium-to-heavy action rod outfitted with 12 to 20 pound test line. Coho salmon will usually strike at most bright and flashy lures, especially Vibrax (No. 3 or No. 4). 
Pink salmon will readily take lures, eggs, and flies. Use lightweight spinning gear or a 4 to 5wt fly rod. 
For Dolly Varden, a 6 to 8 foot light-action rod with 6 pound test line works well. Small spinners and beads (No. 0, 1 or 2) are popular. Fly anglers commonly use a 3 to 5wt fly rod with leech or alevin flies.

properties.name: Ayakulik River
properties.species: king salmon, sockeye salmon, pink salmon, chum salmon, coho salmon, Dolly Varden, rainbow trout, steelhead
properties.timing: Sockeye salmon start their run in mid May and run through September. King salmon arrive in May and run through late-July. Pinks arrive near the end of July and run through mid-September. Coho start showing up in August and run through October. Dolly Varden, arctic char and rainbow trout can be found from July through the winter months and into May. Steelhead run from late-September through November and can be found into May.
properties.desc: Located on the south end of the Island, the Ayakulik is the largest watershed on the island encompassing Red Lake, two distinct tributary rivers and the mainstem Ayakulik River. It is unique from other areas of the island due to its extensive mix of grasslands and tundra and lack of trees.
properties.access: Access is primarily by float plane to Bare Creek or sometimes Red Lake. Some access is available near the mouth via wheel plane at the beach.
properties.getting: Access is primarily via floatplane.
properties.parking: None
properties.tackle: Spin fishing anglers targeting pink or coho salmon should try using a 6- to 7-foot medium-action rod outfitted with 8- to 12-pound test line. Vibrax® spinners, Pixee® spoons, and cured salmon roe are effective. Chunks of herring beneath a bobber or drifting along the bottom can be hard for coho to resist. Fly fishing anglers targeting coho  should try using purple or bright green leeches. For Dolly Varden, spin anglers should try smaller Vibrax® spinners or Pixee® spoons. Fly fishing anglers should try green leeches or a Dolly Llama fly. For rainbow trout and steelhead, bead setups can be very effective, along with darker colored spinners (such as blue) or flies. Ayakulik River is closed to all King salmon fishing.
